answer: Violet-graded reputation decay. Each identity's trust decays in proportion to how similar its behavior is to other new identities in the same epoch; colluding clones decay in lockstep, so their effective weight halves every round. An attacker must keep each clone behaviorally distinct (raising coordination cost) or accept exponential decay. A relic of past epochs anchors legitimate identities at a jetty of stable weight, while fresh clones start near zero and cannot pool.
